chapter_summary: After Jesus rose from the dead, He appeared to seven of His disciples by the Sea of Tiberias. They had fished all night and caught nothing, but Jesus told them to cast the net on the right side — and they caught 153 fish! Jesus had breakfast ready on the shore. He then asked Peter three times, 'Do you love Me?' and three times told him to feed His sheep — gently restoring Peter after Peter had denied Him three times. Jesus also told Peter to follow Him, no matter what happened to anyone else. John ends his Gospel by saying Jesus did so much more than any book could ever hold.
main_lesson: Jesus restores broken people with love and gives them a new purpose — 'Follow Me.'

memory_verse.kjv: He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
memory_verse.little_bible: Jesus asked Peter a third time: 'Peter, do you love Me?' Peter felt sad to be asked again. He said, 'Lord, You know everything. You know I love You.' Jesus said, 'Then feed My sheep.'

parent_guide: John 21 is an epilogue and one of the most tender passages in all of Scripture. The fishing miracle (vv1-14) echoes the original calling of the disciples (Luke 5) — Jesus meeting them in their work, providing abundance where they had nothing. The breakfast scene is quietly domestic and profoundly comforting: the risen Son of God cooking fish on a charcoal fire. The triple restoration of Peter (vv15-17) is the theological and emotional climax. Peter had denied Jesus three times around a charcoal fire (John 18:18, 25-27); here, beside another charcoal fire, Jesus asks three times and Peter answers three times — each exchange healing one denial. Jesus uses two different Greek words for 'love' (agape and phileo), and Peter consistently uses phileo ('I am fond of You'), which may reflect his honest humility after his failure rather than claiming the higher love he once boasted of. Jesus accepts him exactly where he is and re-commissions him. Verses 18-19 hint at Peter's martyrdom (crucifixion) and close with the same call that began it all: 'Follow me.' The John-Peter sidebar (vv20-23) addresses a misunderstood saying about John. Verse 24 identifies the author, and verse 25 closes with a breathtaking statement about the inexhaustible fullness of Jesus. For children: emphasise that Jesus does not give up on people who have failed. He restores. He asks us to love Him — and then to care for others in His name.
application_for_children: Have you ever done something wrong and felt like Jesus could never use you again? Peter felt that way too. He had let Jesus down badly. But Jesus came looking for him, cooked him breakfast, and asked him — three times — 'Do you love Me?' Every time Peter said yes, Jesus gave him a job: take care of My people. Jesus does the same for you. When you fail, come back to Him. He will restore you and give you a new purpose.

verses.kjv: After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he himself.
verses.little_bible: After all this, Jesus appeared again to His disciples. This time it was by the Sea of Tiberias. Here is how it happened.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus appeared to His disciples again. It was by the big lake.
verses.meaning: The risen Jesus did not disappear after one appearance. He kept showing Himself — proving He was truly alive and still with His people. He comes back for us again and again.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for coming back to us again and again.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it wonderful that Jesus kept appearing to His disciples?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus kept showing up for His friends even after the resurrection. How does Jesus keep showing up in your family's life today?
verses.do_it_today: Thank Jesus for one time He showed up for you — in an answered prayer, a kind person, or a quiet peace.
verses.illustration_prompt: A wide shimmering lake at early morning, golden light just touching the water, distant hills in the background. A small group of men on the shore looking out at the water expectantly. Storybook style, warm watercolor palette.

verses.kjv: There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples.
verses.little_bible: Simon Peter was there, and Thomas, and Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, and James and John the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Seven disciples were together by the lake — including Peter, Thomas, and Nathanael.
verses.meaning: Seven disciples — including Thomas who had doubted and Peter who had denied — were gathered together. Jesus would come to all of them, no matter what they had done.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for coming to all Your friends, even imperfect ones.
verses.discussion_question: Why does it matter that Thomas and Peter were both there?
verses.family_discussion: These disciples had all stumbled in some way. How does it encourage you that Jesus still came to be with them?
verses.do_it_today: If you have pulled away from Jesus because of something you did, come back. He is looking for you.
verses.illustration_prompt: Seven men sitting or standing together near a lake shore in early morning light, looking thoughtful and expectant, some mending fishing nets. Warm golden sunrise colors. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing.
verses.little_bible: Peter said, 'I am going fishing.' The others said, 'We are coming with you.' They got into the boat and fished all through the night — but they caught nothing at all.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Peter said, 'I'm going fishing.' The others went with him. They fished all night. They caught nothing.
verses.meaning: Going back to fishing was natural for these men — it was what they knew. But apart from Jesus, even the fishermen came up empty. We need Jesus in every part of life.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I need You in everything I do today.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever worked hard at something and still got nothing?
verses.family_discussion: The disciples worked all night and caught nothing. What does that tell us about trying to do things without Jesus?
verses.do_it_today: Before you start your work today, ask Jesus to be part of it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A fishing boat on a dark, moonlit lake, two or three men leaning over the side pulling at an empty net, expressions of tired disappointment. Dark water, quiet night atmosphere. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.
verses.little_bible: As morning arrived, Jesus was standing on the shore. But the disciples did not know it was Jesus — not yet.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Morning came. Jesus stood on the shore. The disciples did not know it was Him.
verses.meaning: Jesus came right when the night of failure was ending. He stands at the edge of our empty moments, waiting to help — even when we don't recognise Him yet.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me see You even when I don't recognise You at first.
verses.discussion_question: Can Jesus be near you even when you do not notice Him?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus was there on the shore the whole time. How can you look for Jesus in moments when you feel alone or lost?
verses.do_it_today: Look for a moment today where Jesus might be quietly near — even if it seems ordinary.
verses.illustration_prompt: A lone figure standing on a rocky shore in pale morning light, mist over the water, a small boat visible in the distance. The figure is calm and waiting. Storybook style, soft pastel dawn colors.

verses.kjv: Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat? They answered him, No.
verses.little_bible: Jesus called out to them: 'Friends, have you caught any fish?' They called back: 'No.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus called out, 'Have you caught any fish?' They said, 'No.'
verses.meaning: Jesus called them 'children' — a tender, caring word. He already knew the answer, but He asked so they would admit their need. He meets us in our emptiness.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I will be honest with You about my needs.
verses.discussion_question: Why did Jesus ask if they caught fish when He already knew the answer?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus calls us 'children' with love. How does it feel to know Jesus cares about even the small, ordinary things we need?
verses.do_it_today: Tell Jesus honestly about one thing you need today — even a small thing.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure on the shore cupping his hands around his mouth, calling out to men in a boat on golden morning water. The men in the boat look up in surprise. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes.
verses.little_bible: He said, 'Throw your net over the right side of the boat, and you will find fish.' They threw it — and now they could not even pull it in, because there were so many fish!
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, 'Throw the net on the right side.' They did — and it was packed full of fish!
verses.meaning: One word from Jesus changed everything. The same net, the same water, the same men — but now abundance. Obedience to Jesus turns emptiness into overflow.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me obey Your voice and trust Your word.
verses.discussion_question: What changed when the disciples listened to Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: The disciples obeyed even though it seemed odd — and got a miracle. When has obeying God surprised you with something good?
verses.do_it_today: Do one thing today that you know Jesus wants you to do, even if it seems small.
verses.illustration_prompt: Men in a boat straining together to haul an overflowing net bursting with silvery fish from bright morning water, expressions of amazed joy. Golden sunlight sparkling on the lake. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved saith unto Peter, It is the Lord. Now when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his fisher's coat unto him, (for he was naked,) and did cast himself into the sea.
verses.little_bible: John said to Peter, 'It is the Lord!' The moment Peter heard that, he wrapped his outer coat around himself and jumped straight into the water to swim to Jesus.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: John said, 'It's the Lord!' Peter jumped into the water and swam to Jesus!
verses.meaning: John recognised Jesus first, but Peter acted first — he could not wait to get to Jesus. When we truly love Jesus, nothing can hold us back from running to Him.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, make me eager to come to You every day.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think Peter jumped into the water instead of waiting for the boat?
verses.family_discussion: Peter couldn't wait to reach Jesus. What does that eagerness say about how much he loved Jesus? How eager are we to come to Jesus?
verses.do_it_today: Come to Jesus today without delaying — in prayer, right now.
verses.illustration_prompt: A bearded man leaping from the side of a wooden boat into shimmering morning water, arms outstretched, face full of joy and excitement, a figure standing on the distant shore. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: And the other disciples came in a little ship; (for they were not far from land, but as it were two hundred cubits,) dragging the net with fishes.
verses.little_bible: The other disciples came in the boat, dragging the heavy net full of fish. They were not far from shore — only about 100 metres away.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The other disciples came in the boat, dragging the net full of fish to shore.
verses.meaning: Not everyone runs ahead like Peter — some come steadily, doing the work. God uses every kind of person. There is room for the leapers and the steady ones.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, however I come to You, let me come.
verses.discussion_question: Is there anything wrong with coming to Jesus more slowly and steadily, like the other disciples?
verses.family_discussion: Some people in your family might be quiet and steady. Others might be bold and quick. How does God use both kinds of people?
verses.do_it_today: Encourage someone in your family today — even if they are different from you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A small wooden boat moving slowly through morning water, four or five men pulling hard on a bulging net, the shoreline visible ahead. Storybook style, warm colors.

verses.kjv: As soon then as they were come to land, they saw a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread.
verses.little_bible: When they reached the shore, they saw a charcoal fire already burning, with fish cooking on it, and bread ready beside it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: On the shore there was a fire, fish cooking, and bread. Jesus had breakfast ready!
verses.meaning: Jesus had already prepared breakfast. He did not wait for them to bring their catch — He had provided everything they needed. Our Lord is a servant who prepares for us before we arrive.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for preparing good things for me.
verses.discussion_question: What does it tell you about Jesus that He had breakfast ready for tired fishermen?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus served His friends a meal. How does your family show love by serving each other?
verses.do_it_today: Do something kind for someone before they ask — prepare something, help with something, surprise them.
verses.illustration_prompt: A small fire of glowing coals on a sandy shore with fish sizzling over it and a round loaf of bread nearby, early morning light, the lake shimmering in the background. Storybook style, cozy and warm.

verses.kjv: Jesus saith unto them, Bring of the fish which ye have now caught.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said to them, 'Bring some of the fish you just caught.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, 'Bring some of your fish here too.'
verses.meaning: Jesus involved them in the meal even though He had provided everything. He included their catch — what they had given — to honour their work and make the meal shared.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, take what I bring and use it for Your glory.
verses.discussion_question: Why did Jesus ask them to bring fish when He already had fish cooking?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus let the disciples contribute. How does God include what we give — our time, love, work — in His plans?
verses.do_it_today: Offer something you have — a talent, time, or kind action — to help someone today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus standing by the fire with a welcoming gesture toward the men carrying fish from the net, early morning light, a relaxed and joyful scene. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land full of great fishes, an hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, yet was not the net broken.
verses.little_bible: Peter climbed up and dragged the net full of large fish to the shore. They counted them — one hundred and fifty-three fish! And even though there were so many, the net did not tear.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Peter pulled in the net. They counted 153 big fish! The net did not break.
verses.meaning: 153 is exact — John counted and remembered. The net did not break. God's blessing can hold everything He sends, and He sends abundance. Nothing in His provision is wasted.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, Your blessings are always more than enough.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think John remembered the exact number of fish?
verses.family_discussion: The net did not break even with 153 fish. What does that say about God's ability to hold everything He provides?
verses.do_it_today: Count at least three blessings God gave you this week. Write them down.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peter hauling a bulging net overflowing with large silvery fish onto a sunny beach, other disciples counting fish with wide eyes and joyful expressions. Storybook style, bright morning light.

verses.kjv: Jesus saith unto them, Come and dine. And none of the disciples durst ask him, Who art thou? knowing that it was the Lord.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said, 'Come and have breakfast.' None of the disciples dared ask, 'Who are you?' — they already knew it was the Lord.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, 'Come eat!' They all knew it was Jesus. No one had to ask.
verses.meaning: Jesus invited them to eat with Him — a simple, warm, human act. They knew who He was without needing proof. There are moments when we simply know Jesus is present.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I want to be close to You every day.
verses.discussion_question: What does it feel like to have a meal with someone you love? How is that like being with Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus said 'Come and eat' — a moment of warmth and togetherness. How does your family make meals together a time of love?
verses.do_it_today: Make your next family meal a time to be truly present — put devices away and just enjoy each other.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus gesturing welcomingly toward a small fire, disciples gathering around Him smiling, fish and bread spread on the shore, morning sunlight, peaceful and joyful. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: Jesus then cometh, and taketh bread, and giveth them, and fish likewise.
verses.little_bible: Jesus came over, took the bread, and gave it to them. He did the same with the fish.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus gave them bread and fish. He served them Himself.
verses.meaning: The risen Lord of all creation served breakfast to tired fishermen. Jesus is not distant or proud — He comes, He takes, He gives. He still serves us with grace.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for serving me with such love.
verses.discussion_question: Does it surprise you that the risen Jesus served His friends breakfast? Why or why not?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus the King served a meal. What does that teach us about what true greatness looks like?
verses.do_it_today: Serve someone in your home today in a small way — without being asked.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus kneeling by the fire, handing a piece of bread to one disciple and fish to another, a gentle warm expression on His face. Morning light, peaceful scene. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: This is now the third time that Jesus shewed himself to his disciples, after that he was risen from the dead.
verses.little_bible: This was the third time Jesus had appeared to His disciples since He rose from the dead.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: This was the third time Jesus appeared after rising from the dead.
verses.meaning: John marks it carefully: the third appearance. Jesus kept coming back to His people. He does not appear once and leave — He is persistent in love and faithful to His promises.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for never leaving Your people.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important that Jesus appeared to His disciples more than once?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus showed Himself three times. How does knowing Jesus keeps coming back help you trust Him?
verses.do_it_today: Remind yourself: Jesus will never leave you. Say it aloud.
verses.illustration_prompt: The number three written in sand on a beach beside the water, with a sunrise behind it, and disciples in the background sharing a meal. Storybook style, symbolic and warm.

verses.kjv: So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
verses.little_bible: After breakfast, Jesus asked Simon Peter, 'Simon, son of Jonas, do you love Me more than these others do?' Peter said, 'Yes, Lord — You know that I love You.' Jesus said, 'Then feed My lambs.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus asked Peter, 'Do you love Me most?' Peter said, 'Yes, Lord.' Jesus said, 'Feed My lambs.'
verses.meaning: Jesus used Peter's full name — serious and tender. After Peter's three denials, Jesus gave him three chances to say 'I love You.' Each answer came with a mission: care for My people. Love for Jesus shows up in caring for others.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, let my love for You show in how I care for others.
verses.discussion_question: How does loving Jesus and taking care of other people go together?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus asked Peter to care for His lambs — other people who follow Jesus. Who in your family or neighbourhood could you care for better this week?
verses.do_it_today: Do one caring act today for someone who is younger or weaker than you.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus sitting on a rock beside the lake looking kindly at Peter, who is kneeling slightly, holding his chest. The morning sun is warm behind them. A small lamb nearby. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
verses.little_bible: Jesus asked him again: 'Simon, son of Jonas, do you love Me?' Peter answered again: 'Yes, Lord, You know that I love You.' Jesus said, 'Then take care of My sheep.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus asked again, 'Do you love Me?' Peter said, 'Yes!' Jesus said, 'Feed My sheep.'
verses.meaning: The second question. Jesus was not punishing Peter — He was healing him. Each question was undoing one denial. Each answer was a fresh start. Jesus is the God of second chances.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for giving me second chances.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think Jesus asked Peter the same question twice?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus kept asking because He wanted full restoration, not a quick fix. How does your family give each other true forgiveness, not just a quick 'it's fine'?
verses.do_it_today: If there is someone you have only half-forgiven, ask God to help you forgive them fully.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus and Peter again beside the lake, Jesus with a gentle look, Peter's face showing emotion — a mix of sadness and hope. Soft morning light, calm water behind them. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
verses.little_bible: Jesus asked a third time: 'Peter, do you love Me?' Peter felt the pain of being asked again. He said, 'Lord, You know everything. You know that I love You.' Jesus said, 'Then feed My sheep.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus asked a third time. Peter felt sad. He said, 'Lord, You know I love You!' Jesus said, 'Feed My sheep.'
verses.meaning: Three denials, three questions, three answers. Peter's grief was the beginning of healing. He stopped claiming the greatest love and simply trusted Jesus to know his heart. That honest humility is where restoration is complete.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, You know my heart. Please restore and use me.
verses.discussion_question: Why did Peter feel sad when Jesus asked the third time?
verses.family_discussion: Peter stopped boasting about his love and just told Jesus: You know me. How honest are you with Jesus about how you really feel?
verses.do_it_today: Pray honestly to Jesus today — not just nice words, but how you truly feel.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peter with tears in his eyes, hands on his chest, looking at Jesus with deep sincerity. Jesus watching him with complete compassion. Lake and morning sky behind them. Storybook style, emotional and tender.

verses.kjv: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'When you were young, you dressed yourself and went wherever you wanted. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and take you where you do not want to go.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus told Peter: 'When you are old, others will lead you where you do not want to go.'
verses.meaning: Jesus was foretelling that Peter would one day die for His sake — crucified. But He told Peter this not to frighten him, but to honour him. Peter's death would glorify God. Following Jesus may cost everything — and it is still worth it.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me follow You even when it is hard.
verses.discussion_question: Is it easy to follow Jesus every day? What makes it hard sometimes?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus told Peter the truth about the future. How does knowing Jesus walks with us through hard things help us be brave?
verses.do_it_today: Tell Jesus one hard thing you are afraid of, and ask Him to be with you in it.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peter standing tall but looking thoughtful as Jesus speaks quietly to him, a distant look in Peter's eyes as if seeing into the future. Calm lake, early morning. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: This spake he, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith unto him, Follow me.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said this to show how Peter would one day die in a way that would glorify God. Then He simply said to Peter: 'Follow Me.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus was showing how Peter would glorify God. Then Jesus said: 'Follow Me.'
verses.meaning: 'Follow Me' — the same two words that began Peter's journey with Jesus (Matthew 4:19). Now they end it too. A life with Jesus starts and ends with the same call: Follow. Nothing more is needed.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I choose to follow You today.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to 'follow' Jesus in everyday life?
verses.family_discussion: Peter's whole life was framed by two words: 'Follow Me.' What does following Jesus look like in your daily life?
verses.do_it_today: Choose one way to follow Jesus today — in how you speak, act, or treat someone.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus walking ahead on a sunlit path by the lake, turning to look back at Peter with a beckoning gesture. Bright open sky, a sense of journey and purpose. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: Then Peter, turning about, seeth the disciple whom Jesus loved following; which also leaned on his breast at supper, and said, Lord, which is he that betrayeth thee?
verses.little_bible: Peter looked around and saw the disciple Jesus loved — John — following behind. This was the same John who had leaned close to Jesus at the Last Supper and asked who would betray Him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Peter turned and saw John following. John had been at the Last Supper with Jesus.
verses.meaning: Instead of keeping his eyes on Jesus, Peter looked at what John was doing. We all do this — we compare our calling with others. But Jesus has a unique path for each of us.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me follow You and not compare myself to others.
verses.discussion_question: Do you ever wonder if what you have to do is fair compared to what others have to do?
verses.family_discussion: Peter looked at John and got distracted. How can comparing ourselves to others pull us away from what God has called us to do?
verses.do_it_today: Instead of comparing yourself to a friend or sibling today, focus on what God wants you to do.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peter looking over his shoulder at John who is following behind, both on a path by the lake, Jesus walking ahead. Peter's face shows curiosity. Storybook style, warm tones.

verses.kjv: Peter seeing him saith to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do?
verses.little_bible: Peter saw John and asked Jesus: 'Lord, what about him? What will happen to him?'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Peter asked Jesus, 'What about John? What will happen to him?'
verses.meaning: Peter's question was human and understandable — but it was the wrong question. God's plan for someone else is not our business. Each of us has our own assignment.
verses.prayer: Lord, help me trust Your plan for me without worrying about others.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it hard not to compare what happens to us with what happens to others?
verses.family_discussion: Peter wanted to know John's fate. How do you handle it when others seem to have an easier path than you?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one thing you believe God has specifically called you to do — just you.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peter gesturing toward John behind them, asking Jesus a question with a curious expression. Jesus is calm and patient. Lake path setting, morning. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me.
verses.little_bible: Jesus answered: 'If it is My will that he stays until I return, what is that to you? You — follow Me!'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, 'That is not your concern. You — follow Me!'
verses.meaning: Jesus gently but clearly redirected Peter. 'What is that to you?' is not harsh — it is freeing. You do not need to manage anyone else's story. Just follow Jesus. That is enough.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I choose to focus on following You — not others.
verses.discussion_question: How does it help to know you only need to follow Jesus — not manage everyone else's life?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus said 'follow thou me' — just you. How can focusing on your own calling with God bring more peace to your life?
verses.do_it_today: Let go of one worry about someone else today. Give it to Jesus.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus pointing forward along the path with a kind but clear expression, looking at Peter while John is visible behind. Peter looking ahead with dawning understanding. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: Then went this saying abroad among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee?
verses.little_bible: This story spread among the believers, and some said John would never die. But Jesus never said that. He only said, 'What if I want him to stay until I come?' — that does not mean he would not die.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People thought Jesus said John would never die. But Jesus did not say that. People misunderstood.
verses.meaning: Misunderstandings spread fast. It is important to listen carefully to what Jesus actually said — not what people think He said. God's Word must be read carefully.
verses.prayer: Lord, help me understand Your Word correctly and not spread wrong ideas.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to read the Bible carefully and not just repeat what others say about it?
verses.family_discussion: A misunderstanding spread through the whole church. How can your family make sure you understand what the Bible really says?
verses.do_it_today: Read one Bible verse today slowly and carefully — what does it actually say?
verses.illustration_prompt: A group of people whispering to each other in a gathering, some looking confused, with a scroll or book of scripture in the background. Storybook style.

verses.kjv: This is the disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his testimony is true.
verses.little_bible: This is the disciple — John — who is telling all these things and who wrote them down. And we know his testimony is true.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: John wrote all these things. And what he wrote is true.
verses.meaning: John identifies himself as the author and appeals to the community: 'We know this is true.' The Gospel is not myth — it is eyewitness testimony, written down so we can believe.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for giving us the true story of Your life.
verses.discussion_question: Why does it matter that the people who wrote the Bible actually saw what happened?
verses.family_discussion: John was an eyewitness. He saw these things. How does that make the Bible different from other stories?
verses.do_it_today: Thank God for the Bible — a true and faithful record of Jesus.
verses.illustration_prompt: An older man seated at a writing table with a scroll and a quill pen, a peaceful expression on his face, sunlight through a window. Storybook style, warm and scholarly.

verses.kjv: And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen.
verses.little_bible: Jesus did so many other things too. If every one of them were written down, I think the whole world could not hold all the books that would need to be written. Amen.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus did so many things. If all were written down, the world could not hold the books! Amen.
verses.meaning: John ends not with a full stop, but with wonder. Jesus is too great for any book to contain. The Gospel is not the whole story — it is the invitation to know Him who is endless.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are greater than I can imagine. I worship You. Amen.
verses.discussion_question: What does it make you feel to know that Jesus is too wonderful to be fully described?
verses.family_discussion: John ends his book with awe and wonder. What is one thing about Jesus that fills your heart with wonder right now?
verses.do_it_today: Tell someone one amazing thing about Jesus today. Share the wonder.
verses.illustration_prompt: An enormous library with endless shelves of books stretching up into glowing light, and a small child looking up at them with wide eyes of wonder. Storybook style, magnificent and awe-inspiring.
